title: Instrument Approaches
source: Cirrus SR20 POH Supplement — Chapter 3, Normals (Sections 160–200)
intro: Every instrument approach starts the same way in the FMS and cockpit flow. The procedures only begin to differ once the aircraft nears the runway environment, based on what kind of minimums and vertical guidance the approach provides.

considerations.title: Selecting an Approach
considerations.text: Loading an approach lets the system keep navigating the current flight plan; activating it navigates direct to the first fix. Loading the full procedure early ensures all fixes are available.

considerations.title: Hold or Straight-In?
considerations.text: Load the hold if any ambiguity exists — it can be removed later with CLR. Only skip it if ATC has explicitly stated "straight-in."

considerations.title: GPS / SBAS
considerations.text: RNAV/GPS approaches use SBAS when available for lateral/vertical guidance; Baro-VNAV is used if SBAS is unavailable. SBAS is required for LP+V and LPV.

considerations.title: Loss of SBAS
considerations.text: Downgrades (e.g., LPV → LNAV/VNAV) are allowed up to 60 seconds before the FAF. After that point, only a downgrade to LNAV is permitted.

considerations.title: Vectors-to-Final
considerations.text: Activating vectors-to-final removes all fixes outside the FAF and makes the inbound course to the FAF active — confirm ATC's intent first.

considerations.title: Temperature Compensation
considerations.text: The system can adjust waypoint crossing altitudes for cold temperatures if manually enabled with the destination temperature entered.

trunk.detail: Verify/set avionics; line-select the approach procedure and check approach/missed waypoints.
Select the appropriate transition and set minimums (BARO or TEMP COMP).
Load or activate the procedure in the flight plan.
Arm the approach mode / select the guidance appropriate to the loaded procedure.
Target airspeed ~120 kt, seatbelts & shoulder harnesses secure, fuel pump on, mixture set for altitude.
Set Mixture, Airspeed to 100kt, Flaps 50%, Landing checklist to line

branchPrompt: The procedure diverges based on the type of minimums and vertical guidance available for the approach:

types.name: Approach with Vertical Guidance
types.tagline: ILS · LPV · LNAV/VNAV · LNAV+V · LP+V · VOR+V
keyPoints: Vertical path information is available from the FAF to the missed approach point.
ILS, LPV, and LNAV/VNAV use an FAA-approved Decision Altitude (DA).
LNAV+V, LP+V, and VOR+V use an advisory glidepath to a Derived DA (published MDA + 50 ft).

steps.detail: Set Missed Approach altitude
Continuous descent following GP/GS (or advisory glidepath) — never level off before minimums.

steps.step: By 500 ft AGL (Can configure at 1000 ft AGL)
steps.detail: Flaps 100%, final items complete, airspeed VTGT +10.
Announce Stable/Unstable and Clearance Received.
"Approaching minimums" announced.
"Minimums, minimums" — decide Landing or Going miss.

types.name: Approach without Vertical Guidance
types.tagline: LNAV · LP · NDB · LOC · LP · VOR
keyPoints: No vertical guidance is available from the FAF to the missed approach point.
All descents use a Minimum Descent Altitude (MDA).
Descent is planned to reach MDA at or slightly before the Visual Descent Point (VDP).

steps.detail: Set MDA and VS Mode
Pilot-flown V/S from the FAF, planned to arrive at MDA at or slightly before the VDP.
Level at MDA if reached before the VDP — never reach the VDP before the MDA.

steps.step: By 500 ft AGL (Can configure at 1000 ft AGL)
steps.detail: Flaps 100%, final items complete, airspeed VTGT +10.
Announce Stable/Unstable and Clearance Received.
Autopilot off.
"Minimums, minimums" + "Set missed approach altitude."
Decide Landing (if in sight) or Going around / missed approach.

types.name: Circle-to-Land Maneuver
types.tagline: Visual maneuvering to a runway not suited for straight-in
keyPoints: The visual phase of an instrument approach used to align with a runway not suited for a straight-in.
SR20 is Category A, but Category B minimums apply if approach speed exceeds 90 knots.
The entire maneuver must stay within the protected circling area for the approach category.

steps.detail: Follow the procedure for the underlying instrument approach.
Set flaps 50%, 90 kt no later than the circling MDA.
ALT selected to command the flight director/autopilot to level at the circling MDA.
"Minimums, minimums" — "Circling" (any part of airport in sight) or Going around.
Maneuver within the protected area; autopilot must be disengaged before descending below MDA.
Clearance Received.
Only after intercepting a normal visual glidepath — set missed approach altitude, complete flaps/final items by 300 ft AGL.
Announce Stable/Unstable.

types.name: IFR Visual Approach
types.tagline: Conducted under an IFR flight plan, flown visually
keyPoints: Allows the pilot to proceed visually to the airport under an IFR flight plan.
Back up with a line-selectable instrument approach's vertical path whenever one is available.
If none is available, build a visual approach with PROC — obstacle clearance is not provided and is the pilot's responsibility.

steps.detail: Follow a loaded instrument approach for guidance, or construct an approximate 3° visual path via PROC.
100 kt, seatbelts secure, fuel pump on, mixture set for altitude.
Autopilot disengaged.
Flaps 100, Close checklist, Airspeed VTGT +10.
Announce Clearance Received
Announce Stable/Unstable

convergence.step: Not in Sight / Unstable / Cannot Continue
convergence.detail: Announce "Going around" and execute the missed approach or go-around procedure.

comparisonRows.label: Minimums Type
comparisonRows.circling: Circling MDA (Cat A, or Cat B if >90 kt)

comparisonRows.label: Vertical Guidance
comparisonRows.vertical: Continuous GP/GS, or advisory glidepath for +V
comparisonRows.circling: Same as underlying approach, then visual

comparisonRows.label: Level-Off Before Landing
comparisonRows.nonvertical: Yes — may level at MDA until the VDP
comparisonRows.circling: Yes — ALT arms 50 ft prior to circling MDA

comparisonRows.label: Minimums Callout
comparisonRows.nonvertical: "Minimums, minimums" + set missed altitude, decide at VDP
comparisonRows.visual: None — flies to touchdown or go-around

comparisonRows.label: Autopilot Restriction
comparisonRows.vertical: Off no lower than DA/DDA or 200 ft AGL in GP/GS
comparisonRows.nonvertical: Off no lower than MDA or 200 ft AGL in GP/GS
comparisonRows.visual: Disengaged no lower than 1000 ft AGL

comparisonRows.label: Flaps / Landing Checklist
comparisonRows.vertical: To the line by FAF; flaps 100% by 500 ft AGL
comparisonRows.nonvertical: To the line by FAF; flaps 100% by 500 ft AGL
comparisonRows.circling: Flaps held at 50%/90 kt; final items withheld until below MDA
comparisonRows.visual: To the line; flaps 100% by 500 ft AGL

comparisonRows.label: Obstacle Clearance
comparisonRows.circling: Pilot must remain in the protected circling area

comparisonRows.label: Applies To
comparisonRows.vertical: ILS, LPV, LNAV/VNAV, LNAV+V, LP+V, VOR+V
comparisonRows.circling: Any approach flown to a circling MDA
comparisonRows.visual: Visual approach / charted visual flight procedure (CVFP)

classification.title: ICAO Annex 10 Approach Classification
classification.intro: Beyond how United's SR20 procedures are flown, ICAO Annex 10 groups every instrument approach into three categories based on the guidance quality and obstacle protection behind the charted minimums.

categories.name: Precision Approach (PA)
categories.description: Provides certified, continuous precision lateral AND vertical guidance to the runway. Obstacle protection is designed around a Missed Approach Point that occurs exactly at DA.
categories.descendBelow: Yes, momentarily. The missed approach obstacle clearance surface is built assuming the aircraft continues to descend slightly below DA while the pilot recognizes minimums and initiates the climb — this is why a true DA (not a floor) can be flown as a continuous descent.

categories.name: Approach with Vertical Guidance (APV)
categories.examples: LPV · LNAV/VNAV · GPS with vertical · LNAV+V · LP+V · VOR+V
categories.minimum: DA (LPV, LNAV/VNAV) or Derived DA — DDA (advisory +V variants, published MDA + 50 ft)
categories.description: Flown exactly like a precision approach — a stabilized, continuous descent with no level-off — but the underlying obstacle protection is not full precision-approach design. LPV and LNAV/VNAV have dedicated APV vertical protection and use a true DA; the advisory +V variants borrow an MDA-based non-precision approach and add a 50 ft buffer to create the DDA.
categories.descendBelow: No. Unlike a true DA, the DDA's +50 ft buffer exists specifically so the aircraft's momentum through the missed approach does not carry it below the charted MDA obstacle protection.

categories.name: Non-Precision Approach (NPA)
categories.examples: VOR · LOC · ASR · NDB · LP · LNAV
categories.description: No vertical guidance segment from the FAF to the Missed Approach Point — a "dive and drive" technique flown with pilot-selected vertical speed down to the MDA.
categories.descendBelow: No. MDA is a hard floor — the aircraft must level off at or before MDA and may not descend further until the required visual references are in sight, at or before the Visual Descent Point (VDP)/MAP.

downgrades.failure: Loss of SBAS more than 60 sec before the FAF
downgrades.note: The system displays "APR ADVISORY – SBAS VNAV not available. Using Baro VNAV" and flags the VDI; the approach mode annunciation shows in amber if LPV service was required.

downgrades.failure: Loss of SBAS within 60 sec of the FAF (or not restored by the FAF)
downgrades.from: Any SBAS-based approach (LPV, LP, LP+V, LNAV+V)
downgrades.note: Too close to the FAF to safely downgrade to a vertical source — all vertical guidance is removed and the approach reverts to MDA minimums.
Obstacle protection reverts to the non-precision localizer segment; the pilot must level at the (higher) LOC MDA instead of continuing to a DA.

downgrades.failure: Baro-VNAV data invalid (temperature or altitude out of limits)
downgrades.note: The vertical deviation indicator is flagged; LNAV is the only downgrade path this close to or after the FAF.

downgrades.failure: GPS / RAIM fault or satellite signal loss
downgrades.from: Any GPS-based approach (LPV, LNAV/VNAV, LNAV, LP)
downgrades.to: Underlying conventional approach (VOR, NDB, ILS localizer) if loaded, otherwise missed approach
downgrades.note: RNAV overlay approaches can revert to the underlying conventional NAVAID; stand-alone RNAV approaches with no ground-based backup require a missed approach.

downgrades.to: Raw-data or conventional backup NAVAID approach, or missed approach if unavailable
downgrades.note: Always brief a conventional backup when flying an RNAV approach, especially into unfamiliar airports.
